subject: SLA: latency bands, maintenance rollback & credits
messages:
From: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblecloud.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@nimblecloud.com, ethan.park@nimblecloud.com
Date: Fri, 22 Dec 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Draft Order Form / SLA questions

Thanks Aditya — attached are the legal team’s initial redlines to the SLA section of the order form (see Redlines_Nimble_SLA_20281221.pdf). High level asks:

- They want tighter definitions of "availability" to exclude scheduled maintenance only after 72 hours explicit notice, and they want an explicit rollback process when a maintenance causes higher-than-expected errors.
- They propose a 99.9% uptime target for our Dedicated offering and want the service credits to be applied per-region rather than global.
- Concern about our latency language: they’ve asked for latency SLAs for P95 and P99 for text-generation endpoints, and finer billing adjustments if latency bands are exceeded for more than 6 consecutive hours.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide P95/P99 latency targets per model-family and whether we can scope maintenance rollback remedies (temporary config rollback to previous model quantization) as an ops remedy?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

--
Sara Gomez
Head of Procurement, NimbleCloud
Sara.Gomez@nimblecloud.com
+1 415-555-0191

Attachment: Redlines_Nimble_SLA_20281221.pdf (PDF, 132KB)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblecloud.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Dec 2028 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RE: Draft Order Form / SLA questions

Sara — thanks for the summary and PDF. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

- Latency SLAs: we can commit to measured P95 latency bands per model-family for the Dedicated SKU. P99 is trickier as tail latency is workload dependent, but we can provide an SLO-style P99 target with an operational caveat (e.g., "P99 target based on baseline corpus and typical sequence length; deviations subject to joint evaluation").

- Maintenance rollback: we have a standard rollback procedure (config + model checkpoint rollback) that we can offer as an ops-level remedy; legal will need this captured as a discrete "Operational Remediation" clause rather than a monetary credit unless it causes availability breach.

- Service credits: applying credits per-region is feasible if NimbleCloud requires region-scoped billing; it does add complexity to measurement, but we can provide region-level telemetry to support it.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Lauren and Marissa to prepare a redline response and a short one-page summary that maps their asks to our acceptable contract language. Can we book 30 minutes today at 4pm PT to walk through the redlines?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0142

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@nimblecloud.com>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Dec 2028 12:13:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: RE: Draft Order Form / SLA questions

Sara — looping legal and ops heads from our side. Quick notes attached: we put line-by-line suggestions in Redline_diff_summary.xlsx and a short rationale in Proposed-SLA-latency-banding.docx. Highlights: 

- We propose a hybrid approach for P99: contractual "Target" + operational "Investigation & Adjustment" clause that triggers a joint root-cause review and temporary credit hold rather than immediate credits. That preserves a predictable commercial outcome while protecting both sides from noisy tails.

- For maintenance rollback: propose an "Operational Remediation" checkbox with two tracks — rollback (ops-only) and credit (monetary) if the event qualifies as an Availability Incident per the uptime measurement window. We suggest a 6-hour continuity threshold for triggering credit eligibility.

- For region-level credits: propose an optional Annex B (Region Measurement Annex) customers can opt into — it outlines measurement shards, telemetry endpoints, and a per-region credit calculation.

Attaching the files and will be on the 4pm PT call. If that doesn't work, propose Mon 26th 9am PT.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redline_diff_summary.xlsx (Excel, 42KB); Proposed-SLA-latency-banding.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@nimblecloud.com>

Date: Fri, 22 Dec 2028 14:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form / SLA questions

Thanks — Ethan from NimbleCloud ops. Couple of technical clarifications before the call: 

1) For the P95/P99 split, can Redwood provide a per-model-family baseline latency report (sample traces) so our infra team can validate the proposed bands?

2) Regarding rollback: what is the typical RTO (time-to-rollback) and how much state is lost during rollback (KV cache, pending requests)? We want to understand ops impact so we can weigh monetary credit vs. operational remedy.

3) For region-level measurement: do you currently shard token counters and request traces by region/availability-zone? If not, what's the ETA to enable region-scoped telemetry exports?

We prefer to have these clarified in writing in the annex rather than rely solely on verbal commitment.

—Ethan
Ethan Park
SRE Lead, NimbleCloud
ethan.park@nimblecloud.com

Ethan — quick answers and doc commitments ahead of our call: 

- Baseline traces: attached. We’ll produce a per-model-family baseline latency report sampled over typical production workloads (see "Baseline_Traces_Summary.csv" in the drive link). That will include P50/P95/P99 percentiles and sample sequence-length distribution.

- Rollback RTO: typical RTO for a config + model checkpoint rollback is 8-20 minutes depending on batch warmup; KV cache warms over the first 10k token-queries. State lost is effectively in-flight requests (we can retry idempotent requests) and ephemeral KV cache; persistent user data isn't impacted. We can commit to documenting this in Annex C (Operational Remediation Procedures) with explicit RTO ranges and warmup notes.

- Region telemetry: we shard traces by region today for Dedicated customers; we can enable region-scoped telemetry exports to a customer-owned S3 or a secure signed URL within 7 business days of contract execution. We’ll include the ingestion schema in Annex B.

Action items before the call:
1) Aditya: confirm call time (4pm PT).
2) Lauren/Marissa: upload the short annex drafts to the Drive link and a one-page summary mapping Nimble asks to our position.
3) NimbleCloud: flag any redlines that are deal-blocking so we can escalate to legal.

See you on the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
